name: Jargon HR glossary
license: Editorial content. Cite Jargon HR and link to the canonical URL. Not legal advice.

terms.definition: Jargon HR is a rule-based job-description checker that translates hiring jargon, separates hard gates from core skills and nice-to-haves, scores the company on six heuristics, and builds an evidence-backed interview prep list.
terms.zhDef: 行话 HR 是规则驱动的 JD 体检工具：翻译黑话、区分硬门槛与核心要求、做企业六维评分，并生成带原文依据的面试准备清单。
terms.why: It turns a long, euphemistic JD into a small set of decisions: can I apply, what will be tested, and what should I prepare first.
terms.example: Paste a JD and get a verdict, a requirement table, a jargon decoder, market facts, and a tiered prep list.

terms.definition: JD parsing splits a job description into sections, then into atomic requirements that can each be classified, matched, and scored.
terms.zhDef: 把岗位描述先分节、再拆成可分类、可匹配、可评分的原子要求。
terms.why: A single bullet often mixes a hard gate, a tool, and a nice-to-have; treating the bullet as one unit hides which part actually matters.
terms.example: “5+ years Java, Kafka, and a Master’s degree” becomes three requirements with different types and weights.

terms.definition: A market pack is a country-specific bundle of currency parsing, city and legal-form detection, local jargon, statutory facts, and scoring adjustments.
terms.zhDef: 按国家打包的货币、城市/法律实体识别、本土黑话、法定事实与评分调整。
terms.why: Institutions differ; a German Probezeit or a Dutch proeftijd is not the same thing as a UK probation clause.
terms.example: The UK pack knows Right to work and IR35; the German pack knows Probezeit and Tarifvertrag.

terms.definition: An industry overlay adds sector-specific signals and a light scoring adjustment on top of a market pack, without duplicating the country data.
terms.zhDef: 在市场包之上叠加行业信号和轻量评分调整，不复制国家数据。
terms.why: A finance KYC requirement and a healthcare credentialing requirement are different bottlenecks even in the same country.
terms.example: Finance adds KYC/AML/SOX; sales adds quota/commission/territory; public sector adds clearance and GS grades.

terms.definition: The facts layer contains jurisdiction-level defaults such as statutory holiday, pension minimums, notice periods, IR35, Blue Card, and H-1B, each with a source link.
terms.zhDef: 带官方来源的法定默认值，如法定假期、养老金、notice、IR35、Blue Card、H-1B。
terms.why: Facts are stable-ish and verifiable; jargon is probabilistic. Mixing them creates false confidence.
terms.example: The UK pack links GOV.UK and HMRC; the German pack links BUrlG, BGB, and Make it in Germany.

terms.definition: A hard gate is a requirement that can stop an application before skills are assessed, such as work authorization, a required license, a degree level, or a minimum number of years.
terms.zhDef: 在评估能力前就能让申请出局的硬性条件，如工作许可、执照、学历、最低年限。
terms.why: Missing a hard gate makes prep irrelevant until the gate is solved or explicitly waived.
terms.example: “Must have the right to work in the UK” or “Master’s degree required” is a hard gate; “Kafka is a plus” is not.

terms.definition: A core requirement is a capability the role is actually hired for; it usually drives interview depth and leveling, even when the JD does not use the word “required”.
terms.zhDef: 岗位真正招人要看的能力，通常决定面试深度和定级。
terms.why: Core requirements deserve evidence and rehearsal; nice-to-haves only break ties.
terms.example: For a backend role, “owns services end to end” and “expert in Java or Kotlin” are core.

terms.definition: A nice-to-have is a preferred signal that is not expected to be met by every qualified candidate.
terms.zhDef: 不是每个合格候选人都必须具备的偏好项。
terms.why: It should not dominate prep time; it matters as a tie-breaker after hard gates and core skills.
terms.example: “DDD experience” or “payments background” is usually a plus, not a gate.

terms.definition: Prep score = W × Q × Gap. W is the requirement weight, Q is a prior on the probability it gets asked, and Gap combines missing evidence with the ability to explain it.
terms.zhDef: 准备分 = W × Q × Gap：权重 × 被问概率先验 × 证据/表达缺口。
terms.why: It ranks preparation by leverage, not by how scary a bullet sounds.
terms.example: A core requirement with weak evidence and a hard gate both score high, but for different reasons.

terms.definition: An evidence gap means you may have the experience but the JD or your materials contain no concrete proof of it.
terms.zhDef: 可能有经验，但 JD 或你的材料里没有具体证据。
terms.why: Interviewers ask for examples; a claim without a metric, scope, or trade-off is hard to defend.
terms.example: “Worked on Kafka” is weaker than “ran 12 Kafka partitions at 8k events/s with a 200ms p99”.

terms.definition: An articulation gap means the evidence exists but you cannot yet explain it clearly, concisely, or in the interviewer’s language.
terms.zhDef: 证据存在，但还不能清楚、简洁地用面试官的语言讲出来。
terms.why: A strong project with a rambling story still reads as weak signal.
terms.example: You built the system but cannot explain the trade-off between consistency and latency in two minutes.

terms.definition: The company check scores stability, growth, management maturity, workload, pay credibility, and hiring sincerity from signals in the JD.
terms.zhDef: 从 JD 信号给稳定性、成长性、管理成熟度、工作强度、薪资可信度、招聘诚意打分。
terms.why: A role can be a good skill match and still be a bad bet; the six dimensions make that trade-off explicit.
terms.example: Urgent hiring plus a vague scope and no reporting line lowers hiring sincerity and management maturity.

terms.definition: Q is a prior estimate of how likely a requirement is to be probed in an interview, based on its type and how central it is to the role.
terms.zhDef: 某条要求在实际面试中被追问的概率先验。
terms.why: Not every line in a JD is tested; Q keeps the prep list from becoming a 40-item slog.
terms.example: A hard gate may be checked by HR; a core skill is likely to get a deep technical question.

terms.definition: Right to work is the UK employer’s legal duty to check that a person is allowed to work before employment starts; sponsorship changes the check and the candidate pool.
terms.zhDef: 英国雇主在入职前必须核验工作许可；需要 sponsorship 时门槛和候选人范围都会变。
terms.why: It is a hard gate that no amount of technical skill can waive.
terms.example: “Must have the right to work in the UK; no sponsorship” means the role is closed to candidates who need a visa.

terms.definition: IR35 is the UK’s off-payroll working rule set, determining whether a contractor engaged through an intermediary is effectively an employee for tax purposes.
terms.zhDef: 英国 off-payroll 规则，判断通过中介合作的承包商在税务上是否实质为雇员。
terms.why: It changes take-home pay, contract structure, and who bears the compliance burden.
terms.example: A “day rate outside IR35” contract can be worth materially more than an inside-IR35 one.

terms.definition: Probezeit is the German probation period; it is commonly up to six months, and notice during probation can be shorter than the statutory notice after it.
terms.zhDef: 德国试用期，常见最长 6 个月；试用期内的解约通知期可能短于正式期。
terms.why: It is the easiest exit for either side, and it changes how much notice you have.
terms.example: A six-month Probezeit with two weeks’ notice is a different risk from a permanent contract with three months’ notice.

terms.definition: Kündigungsfrist is the German notice period; the statutory baseline is four weeks to the end of a month, but a contract or Tarifvertrag can extend it.
terms.zhDef: 德国解约通知期；法定基线是月底前 4 周，合同或集体协议可以延长。
terms.why: Notice affects start dates, visa timing, and how quickly you can leave a bad role.
terms.example: “3 Monate zum Quartalsende” means three months to the end of a quarter, not three months from today.

terms.definition: A Tarifvertrag is a collective agreement between an employer or employers’ association and a union, setting pay, hours, leave, and other terms.
terms.zhDef: 德国雇主/雇主协会与工会签订的集体协议，规定薪资、工时、假期等。
terms.why: It can improve or constrain the offer beyond the individual contract, and it is a stability signal.
terms.example: A Tarifvertrag may add 13th-month pay, extra holiday, or a works council framework.

terms.definition: CDI is the French permanent employment contract; CDD is a fixed-term contract with legally limited renewal and termination rules.
terms.zhDef: CDI 是法国长期合同，CDD 是有严格续签/终止规则的短期合同。
terms.why: The contract type changes stability, loan eligibility, notice, and what “permanent” means in the offer.
terms.example: A CDD with a six-month term is not equivalent to a CDI even if the day-to-day work is the same.

terms.definition: RTT (réduction du temps de travail) is extra paid time off earned by employees whose working time exceeds the statutory 35-hour week.
terms.zhDef: 法国每周超过 35 小时法定工时后累积的额外带薪假。
terms.why: It can add 10–20 days off per year, and it is often omitted from English summaries of the offer.
terms.example: A 39-hour contract may come with around 12 RTT days on top of five weeks’ holiday.

terms.definition: A CAO (collectieve arbeidsovereenkomst) is a Dutch collective labour agreement that sets minimum terms for a sector or company.
terms.zhDef: 荷兰行业或公司的集体劳动协议，规定该领域的最低雇佣条件。
terms.why: It can override or supplement the individual contract, including pay scales, leave, and probation.
terms.example: “CAO applies” means the offer is not fully negotiable on every term.

terms.definition: Proeftijd is the Dutch probation period; it is capped at two months for a permanent contract, one month for a fixed term of 6–24 months, and is not allowed for contracts under six months.
terms.zhDef: 荷兰试用期；长期合同最多 2 个月，6–24 个月合同最多 1 个月，6 个月以下不得约定。
terms.why: An illegal or overlong probation clause is a red flag and may be unenforceable.
terms.example: A two-month proeftijd on a one-year contract is longer than the statutory maximum.

terms.definition: Vakantiegeld is the Dutch holiday allowance, usually 8% of gross annual salary, typically paid in May or June.
terms.zhDef: 荷兰假期津贴，通常为年薪的 8%，多在 5/6 月发放。
terms.why: It is a real part of total compensation and is often left out of English salary comparisons.
terms.example: A €60,000 salary plus 8% vakantiegeld is roughly €64,800 gross before other allowances.

terms.definition: The 30% ruling is a Dutch tax facility for eligible incoming employees, allowing a portion of salary to be paid tax-free; the rate and conditions have changed over time.
terms.zhDef: 荷兰针对符合条件的外籍员工的税收优惠，部分薪资可免税；比例和条件会调整。
terms.why: It materially changes net pay and is often mentioned in offers without explaining eligibility.
terms.example: “30% ruling possible” is not a guarantee; the employer and employee must meet the conditions.

terms.definition: The EU Blue Card is a work-and-residence permit for qualified non-EU workers, with salary and qualification thresholds set by the member state.
terms.zhDef: 面向非欧盟高技能人才的欧盟工作/居留许可，薪资和学历门槛由各成员国设定。
terms.why: It is a hard gate for non-EU candidates, and the employer usually has to drive the application.
terms.example: A German Blue Card requires a recognized qualification and a salary above the annual threshold.

terms.definition: At-will employment means either the employer or the employee can end the relationship at any time for any lawful reason, subject to exceptions and contracts.
terms.zhDef: 美国自由雇佣：雇主或员工可在合法范围内随时终止关系，除非合同/法律另有规定。
terms.why: It changes job security and severance expectations compared with notice-based systems.
terms.example: “At-will” does not mean anything goes; anti-discrimination and contract terms still apply.

terms.zh: 雇员 vs 独立承包商
terms.definition: W-2 workers are employees with payroll withholding and benefits; 1099 workers are independent contractors responsible for their own taxes and benefits.
terms.zhDef: W-2 是雇员（代扣税、福利），1099 是独立承包商（自行报税、无福利）。
terms.why: The same headline rate can be worth very different amounts after taxes, benefits, and unpaid time.
terms.example: A 1099 role at $80/hour may net less than a W-2 role at $60/hour with benefits.

terms.definition: A 401(k) is a US employer-sponsored retirement account; employer matching is part of compensation but often vests over time.
terms.zhDef: 美国雇主提供的退休账户；雇主 match 属于薪酬，但通常有归属期。
terms.why: Match and vesting can add meaningful value that a base-salary comparison misses.
terms.example: A 5% match on a $150,000 salary is $7,500 a year before growth.

terms.definition: The H-1B is a US specialty-occupation work visa; it is subject to an annual cap and a lottery, and the employer files the petition.
terms.zhDef: 美国高技能专业岗位工作签证，有年度配额和抽签，由雇主提交申请。
terms.why: It is a hard gate with timing risk; “we sponsor” is not the same as “we will file this year”.
terms.example: A role that requires H-1B sponsorship may be closed even if the technical match is strong.

terms.definition: 抗压 literally means “stress resistance”; in Chinese JDs it often signals high pressure, long hours, or frequent priority changes without saying so directly.
terms.zhDef: “抗压”字面是承受压力，JD 里常暗示高压、长工时或频繁变需求。
terms.why: It is a workload signal, not a personality requirement; ask what a normal week looks like.
terms.example: “抗压能力强，能适应快节奏” is a prompt to ask about hours, on-call, and deadline frequency.

terms.definition: 五险一金 is the Chinese statutory social-insurance and housing-fund package: pension, medical, unemployment, work injury, maternity, and the housing provident fund.
terms.zhDef: 中国法定社保与住房公积金：养老、医疗、失业、工伤、生育 + 公积金。
terms.why: It is a large part of real compensation, and the contribution base matters more than the headline salary.
terms.example: “五险一金全额缴纳” is stronger than “按最低基数缴纳”.

terms.definition: 统招 refers to full-time higher-education admission through the national entrance exam; many Chinese JDs use it as a hard degree filter.
terms.zhDef: 通过全国统一招生考试的全日制学历；很多 JD 把它当硬性学历筛选。
terms.why: It can screen out otherwise qualified candidates, including many self-taught or part-time-degree engineers.
terms.example: “统招本科及以上” is a gate that may be stricter than “本科及以上”.

terms.definition: 大小周 is a schedule that alternates a five-day week and a six-day week, usually without extra pay.
terms.zhDef: 一周双休、一周单休交替的工作节奏，通常没有额外报酬。
terms.why: It adds roughly two extra working days a month and is a concrete workload signal.
terms.example: “大小周” means you should ask which weeks are six-day and whether overtime is paid.
